#!/bin/sh
# =============================================================================
#  pick-model.sh -- single-file launcher for the llama.cpp server commands
#
#  EDITING: all launch commands live in the COMMANDS string near the top of
#  this file. Add, remove or change lines there; the menu adapts
#  automatically because the string is re-read from this file each time the
#  script starts.
#
#  Rules for the COMMANDS string:
#    * one command per line (no backslash line continuations)
#    * blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored
#    * the string is a quoted heredoc (<<'COMMANDS_EOF'), so its contents
#      are taken completely literally: single quotes, double quotes, $ and
#      backticks are all safe inside it
#
#  The selected command is executed VERBATIM by sh: no parameter is ever
#  parsed, reordered or modified, so the commands work exactly as written.
#
#  Usage:
#    ./pick-model.sh            interactive menu
#    ./pick-model.sh 3          run command number 3 directly
#    ./pick-model.sh gemma      run the command containing "gemma"
#                               (case-insensitive); if several commands
#                               match, a menu narrowed to them is shown
#
#  Inside the menu you can type:
#    number          run that command
#    text fragment   narrow the list to matching commands (case-insensitive);
#                    a unique match runs immediately
#    r               show all commands again (clears the narrowing)
#    e               show where to edit the COMMANDS string
#    q               quit
#
#  The commands use relative paths (./cuda/..., ./models/...), so this
#  script always starts from the directory it lives in.
# =============================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  COMMANDS -- edit this block freely (one command per line)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
COMMANDS=$(cat <<'COMMANDS_EOF'
./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-F16-qwen3.8-27B.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --image-min-tokens 1024 -ngl 99 -sm tensor -fit off -c 262144 -b 512 -ub 512 --reasoning-preserve -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B-f16.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --image-min-tokens 1024 -ngl 99 -sm tensor -fit off -c 262144 -b 512 -ub 512 --reasoning-preserve -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/Qwen3.8-27B-pi-Q4_K_M.gguf -md ./models/mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-pi-Q4_0.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-Qwen3.8-27B-pi-BF16.gguf --spec-draft-n-max 3 --image-min-tokens 1024 -ngl 99 -sm tensor -fit off -c 262144 -b 512 -ub 512 --reasoning-preserve -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/gemma-4-31B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-BF16_gemma31b.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --model-draft ./models/mtp-gemma-4-31B-it.gguf --spec-draft-n-max 3 -ngl 99 -c 32768 -b 256 -ub 256 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/gemma-4-12b-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --model-draft ./models/mtp-gemma-4-12b-it.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-BF16.gguf -c 262144 -ngl 999 -sm layer -ts 1,1 -fa 1 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 12 -np 1 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --reasoning-budget 0 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'
COMMANDS_EOF
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Script body -- nothing below this line normally needs to be changed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

set -u

# Run from this script's directory (the commands use ./cuda and ./models).
SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd) || exit 1
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR" || exit 1
SELF="$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")"
EDIT_LINE=$(awk '/^COMMANDS=/ { print NR; exit }' "$SELF")

LINES=$(mktemp 2>/dev/null) || LINES="./.pick-model-tmp.$$"
: > "$LINES" || exit 1
trap 'rm -f "$LINES"' EXIT INT TERM

# FILTER: active text narrowing ('' = all commands).
FILTER=''
TOTAL=0

# filter_list [pattern]
# Rebuilds $LINES from the COMMANDS string. Without a pattern it contains
# all command lines; with a pattern only the lines that contain it
# (case-insensitive). Updates TOTAL.
filter_list() {
    if [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$COMMANDS" | awk '
            { sub(/\r$/, "") }          # CRLF safety only, nothing else
            /^[ \t]*$/                  { next }   # skip blank lines
            /^[ \t]*#/                  { next }   # skip comments
            { print }
        ' > "$LINES"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$COMMANDS" | awk -v q="$1" '
            BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
            { sub(/\r$/, "") }
            /^[ \t]*$/                  { next }
            /^[ \t]*#/                  { next }
            q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print }
        ' > "$LINES"
    fi
    TOTAL=$(wc -l < "$LINES" | tr -d '[:space:]')
}

filter_list ''
if [ "$TOTAL" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "error: no launch commands found in the COMMANDS string at the top." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# model_label <line>
# Prints the value of the -m flag of <line>, or the program name if -m is
# absent. Used only for the menu display; the command itself is untouched.
model_label() {
    lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/.*[[:space:]]\{1,\}-m[[:space:]]\{1,\}\([^[:space:]]\{1,\}\).*/\1/p')
    if [ -z "$lbl" ]; then
        lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '{print $1}')
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$lbl"
}

# short <maxchars> <text>
# Prints <text> truncated to <maxchars> characters (with "..." when cut).
short() {
    t=$(printf '%s' "$2" | cut -c1-"$1")
    if [ "$(printf '%s' "$2" | wc -c | tr -d '[:space:]')" -gt "$1" ]; then
        t="$t..."
    fi
    printf '%s' "$t"
}

# line_for_number <n>
# Prints line number <n> (1-based) of the current list; empty if out of range.
line_for_number() {
    case $1 in
        '' | *[!0-9]*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    if [ "$1" -ge 1 ] && [ "$1" -le "$TOTAL" ]; then
        sed -n "$1p" "$LINES"
    fi
}

# print_menu
# Lists the current (possibly narrowed) command list.
print_menu() {
    if [ -z "$FILTER" ]; then
        echo "Available commands ($TOTAL):"
    else
        echo "Commands matching '$FILTER' ($TOTAL):"
    fi
    echo
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        lbl=$(model_label "$line")
        printf ' %2d) %s\n' "$i" "${lbl##*/}"
        printf '      %s\n' "$(short 110 "$line")"
    done < "$LINES"
    echo
    echo "  number or text: select/narrow    r: show all    e: edit location    q: quit"
    echo
}

# resolve_choice <choice>
# Chooses a command from the current list in $LINES.
# Returns: 0 = one command selected (CHOSEN_N/CHOSEN_LINE set),
#          2 = several matches: $LINES narrowed to them, FILTER updated,
#          1 = no match or invalid input.
resolve_choice() {
    CHOSEN_N=''
    CHOSEN_LINE=''
    case $1 in
        *[!0-9]*)   # text fragment: search the current list, case-insensitive
            n=$(awk -v q="$1" 'BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
                q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print NR }' "$LINES")
            if [ -z "$n" ]; then
                echo "No command matches '$1'."
                return 1
            fi
            count=$(printf '%s\n' "$n" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')
            if [ "$count" -eq 1 ]; then
                CHOSEN_N=$n
                CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$CHOSEN_N")
                return 0
            fi
            # several matches: narrow the list to exactly those lines
            filter_list "$1"
            FILTER=$1
            echo "Narrowed to $TOTAL matching commands."
            return 2
            ;;
        *)          # explicit number in the current list
            CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$1")
            if [ -z "$CHOSEN_LINE" ]; then
                echo "Invalid selection (expected 1-$TOTAL)."
                return 1
            fi
            CHOSEN_N=$1
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
}

# run_selected
# Prints what is about to run, then starts it with sh exactly as written.
run_selected() {
    echo
    echo "Running #$CHOSEN_N -- $(model_label "$CHOSEN_LINE"):"
    echo "  $CHOSEN_LINE"
    echo
    exec sh -c "$CHOSEN_LINE"
}

# --- Optional direct selection from the command line -----------------------
if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    resolve_choice "$1"
    rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
        run_selected
    fi
    # rc 1/2: fall through to the menu (the list may now be narrowed)
fi

# --- Interactive menu loop --------------------------------------------------
while :; do
    print_menu
    printf 'Select a number or text fragment (r: show all, e: edit, q: quit): '
    read -r choice || exit 0
    case $choice in
        q | Q | quit) exit 0 ;;
        e | E)
            echo
            echo "Edit the COMMANDS string (line $EDIT_LINE) in:"
            echo "  $SELF"
            echo
            ;;
        r | R)
            FILTER=''
            filter_list ''
            ;;
        '') continue ;;
        *)
            resolve_choice "$choice"
            rc=$?
            if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
                run_selected
            fi
            echo
            ;;
    esac
done

#!/bin/sh
# pick-model.sh
#
# Interactive launcher for the llama.cpp commands stored in launcher.sh.
#
# How it works:
#   * On every start it re-reads the command file, so any command you add,
#     remove or comment out is picked up immediately ("real time") — this
#     script never needs to be updated when the command list changes.
#   * The selected command is executed verbatim: the exact line text is
#     passed to sh, so no parameter is ever parsed, reordered or modified.
#   * Commands must be one line each (no backslash continuations).
#     Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored.
#
# Usage:
#   ./pick-model.sh            show the menu and pick interactively
#   ./pick-model.sh 3          run command number 3 directly
#   ./pick-model.sh gemma      run the single command containing "gemma"
#                              (case-insensitive); if several match, the
#                              menu is shown instead
#
# The command file defaults to launcher.sh next to this script;
# override with the environment variable LLAMA_COMMANDS.

set -u

# Commands use relative paths (./cuda/llama-server, ./models/...),
# so always run from the directory that contains this script.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1

COMMAND_FILE="${LLAMA_COMMANDS:-launcher.sh}"

if [ ! -f "$COMMAND_FILE" ]; then
    echo "error: command file '$COMMAND_FILE' not found in $(pwd)." >&2
    echo "       Add your llama-server commands there, one per line." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Working copy containing only executable lines, in original order.
# (awk guarantees a trailing newline per line, even if the source file
# lacks one on its last line.)
LINES=$(mktemp 2>/dev/null) || LINES="./.pick-model-tmp.$$"
: > "$LINES" || exit 1
trap 'rm -f "$LINES"' EXIT INT TERM

awk '{
    sub(/\r$/, "")                      # CRLF safety only
    if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*$/) next           # skip blank lines
    if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*#/) next           # skip comments (incl. shebang)
    print
}' "$COMMAND_FILE" > "$LINES"

TOTAL=$(wc -l < "$LINES" | tr -d '[:space:]')
if [ "$TOTAL" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "error: no launch commands found in $COMMAND_FILE." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# model_label <line>
# Prints the value of the -m flag, or the program name if -m is absent.
model_label() {
    lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/.*[[:space:]]\{1,\}-m[[:space:]]\{1,\}\([^[:space:]]\{1,\}\).*/\1/p')
    if [ -z "$lbl" ]; then
        lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '{print $1}')
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$lbl"
}

# short <maxchars> <text>
# Prints <text> truncated to <maxchars> (with an ellipsis when cut).
short() {
    t=$(printf '%s' "$2" | cut -c1-"$1")
    if [ "$(printf '%s' "$2" | wc -c | tr -d '[:space:]')" -gt "$1" ]; then
        t="$t..."
    fi
    printf '%s' "$t"
}

# line_for_number <n>
# Prints line number <n> (1-based) from the command list; empty if out of range.
line_for_number() {
    case $1 in
        '' | *[!0-9]*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    if [ "$1" -ge 1 ] && [ "$1" -le "$TOTAL" ]; then
        sed -n "$1p" "$LINES"
    fi
}

# print_menu
# Shows all commands with a number and the model they load.
print_menu() {
    echo "Available commands in $COMMAND_FILE ($TOTAL):"
    echo
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        lbl=$(model_label "$line")
        printf ' %2d) %s\n' "$i" "${lbl##*/}"
        printf '      %s\n' "$(short 110 "$line")"
    done < "$LINES"

model_label() {
    lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/.*[[:space:]]\{1,\}-m[[:space:]]\{1,\}\([^[:space:]]\{1,\}\).*/\1/p')
    if [ -z "$lbl" ]; then
        lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '{print $1}')
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$lbl"

short() {
    t=$(printf '%s' "$2" | cut -c1-"$1")
    if [ "$(printf '%s' "$2" | wc -c | tr -d '[:space:]')" -gt "$1" ]; then
        t="$t..."
    fi
    printf '%s' "$t"
}

# line_for_number <n>
# Prints line number <n> (1-based) of the command list; empty if out of range.
line_for_number() {
    case $1 in
        '' | *[!0-9]*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    if [ "$1" -ge 1 ] && [ "$1" -le "$TOTAL" ]; then
        sed -n "$1p" "$LINES"
    fi
}

# print_menu
# Lists all commands with a number and the model each one loads.
print_menu() {
    echo "Available commands ($TOTAL):"
    echo
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        lbl=$(model_label "$line")
        printf ' %2d) %s\n' "$i" "${lbl##*/}"
        printf '      %s\n' "$(short 110 "$line")"
    done < "$LINES"
    echo
    echo "  q: quit    e: show where to edit the COMMANDS block"
    echo
}

# resolve_choice <choice>
# Turns a number or a text fragment into CHOSEN_N / CHOSEN_LINE.
# Succeeds only when exactly one command is selected.
resolve_choice() {
    CHOSEN_N=''
    CHOSEN_LINE=''
    case $1 in
        *[!0-9]*)   # text fragment: search all commands, case-insensitive
            n=$(awk -v q="$1" 'BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
                q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print NR }' "$LINES")
            if [ -z "$n" ]; then
                echo "No command matches '$1'."
                return 1
            fi
            count=$(printf '%s\n' "$n" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')
            if [ "$count" -gt 1 ]; then
                echo "Several commands match '$1' (numbers: $(printf '%s ' $n)). Pick one:"
                return 1
            fi
            CHOSEN_N=$n
            ;;
        *)          # explicit number
            CHOSEN_N=$1
            ;;
    esac
    CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$CHOSEN_N")
    if [ -z "$CHOSEN_LINE" ]; then
        echo "Invalid selection."
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# run_selected
# Prints what is about to run, then starts it with sh exactly as written.
run_selected() {
    echo
    echo "Running #$CHOSEN_N -- $(model_label "$CHOSEN_LINE"):"
    echo "  $CHOSEN_LINE"
    echo
    exec sh -c "$CHOSEN_LINE"
}

# --- Optional direct selection from the command line -----------------------
if [ "$#" -ge 1 ] && resolve_choice "$1"; then
    run_selected
fi

# --- Interactive menu loop --------------------------------------------------
# (The COMMANDS block was re-read from this file at startup, so the menu
# always reflects the file's current contents: edit the block, re-run.)
while :; do
    print_menu
    printf 'Select a number, a fragment of the command, or q to quit: '
    read -r choice || exit 0
    case $choice in
        q | Q | quit) exit 0 ;;
        e | E)
            echo
            echo "Edit the COMMANDS block (between the BEGIN/END markers) at the top of:"
            echo "  $SELF"
            echo
            ;;
        '') continue ;;
    esac
    if resolve_choice "$choice"; then
        run_selected
    fi
    echo
done
"}

#!/bin/sh
# =============================================================================
#  pick-model.sh -- single-file launcher for the llama.cpp server commands
#
#  EDITING: all launch commands live in the COMMANDS string near the top of
#  this file. Add, remove or change lines there; the menu adapts
#  automatically because the string is re-read from this file each time the
#  script starts.
#
#  Rules for the COMMANDS string:
#    * one command per line (no backslash line continuations)
#    * blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored
#    * the string is a quoted heredoc (<<'COMMANDS_EOF'), so its contents
#      are taken completely literally: single quotes, double quotes, $ and
#      backticks are all safe inside it
#
#  The selected command is executed VERBATIM by sh: no parameter is ever
#  parsed, reordered or modified, so the commands work exactly as written.
#
#  Usage:
#    ./pick-model.sh            interactive menu
#    ./pick-model.sh 3          run command number 3 directly
#    ./pick-model.sh gemma      run the command containing "gemma"
#                               (case-insensitive); if several commands
#                               match, a menu narrowed to them is shown
#
#  Inside the menu you can type a number, a text fragment (narrows the
#  list), r to show all commands again, e for the edit location, q to quit.
#
#  The commands use relative paths (./cuda/..., ./models/...), so this
#  script always starts from the directory it lives in.
# =============================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  COMMANDS -- edit this block freely (one command per line)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
COMMANDS=$(cat <<'COMMANDS_EOF'
... (same 5 lines)
COMMANDS_EOF
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Script body -- nothing below this line normally needs to be changed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

set -u

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd) || exit 1
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR" || exit 1
SELF="$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")"
EDIT_LINE=$(awk '/^COMMANDS=/ { print NR; exit }' "$SELF")

LINES=$(mktemp 2>/dev/null) || LINES="./.pick-model-tmp.$$"
: > "$LINES" || exit 1
trap 'rm -f "$LINES"' EXIT INT TERM

FILTER=''
TOTAL=0

# filter_list [pattern]
# Rebuilds $LINES from the COMMANDS string. Without a pattern it contains
# all command lines; with a pattern only the lines that contain the pattern
# (case-insensitive). Updates TOTAL.
filter_list() {
    if [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$COMMANDS" | awk '
            { sub(/\r$/, "") }
            /^[ \t]*$/ { next }
            /^[ \t]*#/ { next }
            { print }
        ' > "$LINES"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$COMMANDS" | awk -v q="${1}" '
            BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
            { sub(/\r$/, "") }
            /^[ \t]*$/ { next }
            /^[ \t]*#/ { next }
            q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print }
        ' > "$LINES"
    fi
    TOTAL=$(wc -l < "$LINES" | tr -d '[:space:]')
}

filter_list ''
if [ "$TOTAL" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "error: no launch commands found in the COMMANDS string at the top." >&2
    exit 1
fi

model_label() { ... }
short() { ... }
line_for_number() { ... }

print_menu() {
    if [ -z "$FILTER" ]; then
        echo "Available commands ($TOTAL):"
    else
        echo "Commands matching '$FILTER' ($TOTAL):"
    fi
    echo
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        lbl=$(model_label "$line")
        printf ' %2d) %s\n' "$i" "${lbl##*/}"
        printf '      %s\n' "$(short 110 "$line")"
    done < "$LINES"
    echo
    echo "  number or text: select/narrow    r: show all    e: edit location    q: quit"
    echo
}

# resolve_choice <choice>
# Chooses from the current list in $LINES (which may be narrowed by FILTER).
# Returns: 0 = one command selected (CHOSEN_N/CHOSEN_LINE set),
#          2 = several matches: $LINES narrowed to them (FILTER updated),
#          1 = no match / invalid input.
resolve_choice() {
    CHOSEN_N=''
    CHOSEN_LINE=''
    case $1 in
        *[!0-9]*)
            n=$(awk -v q="$1" 'BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
                q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print NR }' "$LINES")
            if [ -z "$n" ]; then
                echo "No command matches '$1'."
                return 1

            count=$(printf '%s\n' "$n" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')
            if [ "$count" -eq 1 ]; then
                CHOSEN_N=$n
                CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$CHOSEN_N")
                return 0
            fi
            filter_list "$1"
            FILTER=$1
            echo "Narrowed to $TOTAL matching commands."
            return 2
            ;;
        *)
            CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$1")
            if [ -z "$CHOSEN_LINE" ]; then
                echo "Invalid selection (expected 1-$TOTAL)."
                return 1
            fi
            CHOSEN_N=$1
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
}

run_selected() {
    echo
    echo "Running #$CHOSEN_N -- $(model_label "$CHOSEN_LINE"):"
    echo "  $CHOSEN_LINE"
    echo
    exec sh -c "$CHOSEN_LINE"
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    resolve_choice "$1"
    rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
        run_selected

fi

while :; do
    print_menu
    printf 'Select a number or text fragment (r: show all, q: quit): '

        e | E)

            ;;
        '') continue ;;
    esac
    resolve_choice "$choice"
    rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
        run_selected
    fi
    echo
done

# =============================================================================
#  pick-model.sh -- single-file launcher for the llama.cpp server commands
#
#  EDITING: all launch commands live in the COMMANDS string near the top of
#  this file. Add, remove or change lines there; the menu adapts

#  script starts.
#
#  Rules for the COMMANDS string:
#    * one command per line (no backslash line continuations)
#    * blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored
#    * the string is a quoted heredoc (<<'COMMANDS_EOF'), so its contents
#      are taken completely literally: single quotes, double quotes, $ and

#  The selected command is executed VERBATIM by sh: no parameter is ever

#
#  Usage:
#    ./pick-model.sh            interactive menu
#    ./pick-model.sh 3          run command number 3 directly
#    ./pick-model.sh gemma      run the command containing "gemma"
#                               (case-insensitive); if several commands
#                               match, a menu narrowed to them is shown
#
#  Inside the menu you can type:
#    number          run that command
#    text fragment   narrow the list to matching commands (case-insensitive);
#                    a unique match runs immediately
#    r               show all commands again (clears the narrowing)
#    e               show where to edit the COMMANDS string
#    q               quit
#
#  The commands use relative paths (./cuda/..., ./models/...), so this
#  script always starts from the directory it lives in.
# =============================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  COMMANDS -- edit this block freely (one command per line)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
COMMANDS=$(cat <<'COMMANDS_EOF'
./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-F16-qwen3.8-27B.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --image-min-tokens 1024 -ngl 99 -sm tensor -fit off -c 262144 -b 512 -ub 512 --reasoning-preserve -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/Qwen3.8-27B-pi-Q4_K_M.gguf -md ./models/mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-pi-Q4_0.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-Qwen3.8-27B-pi-BF16.gguf --spec-draft-n-max 3 --image-min-tokens 1024 -ngl 99 -sm tensor -fit off -c 262144 -b 512 -ub 512 --reasoning-preserve -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/gemma-4-31B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-BF16_gemma31b.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --model-draft ./models/mtp-gemma-4-31B-it.gguf --spec-draft-n-max 3 -ngl 99 -c 32768 -b 256 -ub 256 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/gemma-4-12b-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --model-draft ./models/mtp-gemma-4-12b-it.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-BF16.gguf -c 262144 -ngl 999 -sm layer -ts 1,1 -fa 1 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 12 -np 1 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --reasoning-budget 0 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'

)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Script body -- nothing below this line normally needs to be changed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

set -u

# Run from this script's directory (the commands use ./cuda and ./models).
SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd) || exit 1
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR" || exit 1
SELF="$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")"
EDIT_LINE=$(awk '/^COMMANDS=/ { print NR; exit }' "$SELF")

LINES=$(mktemp 2>/dev/null) || LINES="./.pick-model-tmp.$$"
: > "$LINES" || exit 1
trap 'rm -f "$LINES"' EXIT INT TERM

# FILTER: active text narrowing ('' = all commands).
FILTER=''
TOTAL=0

# filter_list [pattern]
# Rebuilds $LINES from the COMMANDS string. Without a pattern it contains
# all command lines; with a pattern only the lines that contain it
# (case-insensitive). Updates TOTAL.
filter_list() {
    if [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$COMMANDS" | awk '
            { sub(/\r$/, "") }          # CRLF safety only, nothing else
            /^[ \t]*$/                  { next }   # skip blank lines
            /^[ \t]*#/                  { next }   # skip comments

        ' > "$LINES"
    else

            BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
            { sub(/\r$/, "") }
            /^[ \t]*$/                  { next }
            /^[ \t]*#/                  { next }
            q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print }
        ' > "$LINES"
    fi

filter_list ''

    echo "error: no launch commands found in the COMMANDS string at the top." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# model_label <line>
# Prints the value of the -m flag of <line>, or the program name if -m is
# absent. Used only for the menu display; the command itself is untouched.
model_label() {
    lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/.*[[:space:]]\{1,\}-m[[:space:]]\{1,\}\([^[:space:]]\{1,\}\).*/\1/p')
    if [ -z "$lbl" ]; then
        lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '{print $1}')
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$lbl"

# short <maxchars> <text>
# Prints <text> truncated to <maxchars> characters (with "..." when cut).
short() {
    t=$(printf '%s' "$2" | cut -c1-"$1")
    if [ "$(printf '%s' "$2" | wc -c | tr -d '[:space:]')" -gt "$1" ]; then
        t="$t..."
    fi
    printf '%s' "$t"
}

# line_for_number <n>
# Prints line number <n> (1-based) of the current list; empty if out of range.
line_for_number() {
    case $1 in
        '' | *[!0-9]*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    if [ "$1" -ge 1 ] && [ "$1" -le "$TOTAL" ]; then
        sed -n "$1p" "$LINES"
    fi
}

# print_menu
# Lists the current (possibly narrowed) command list.
print_menu() {
    if [ -z "$FILTER" ]; then
        echo "Available commands ($TOTAL):"
    else
        echo "Commands matching '$FILTER' ($TOTAL):"
    fi
    echo
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        lbl=$(model_label "$line")
        printf ' %2d) %s\n' "$i" "${lbl##*/}"
        printf '      %s\n' "$(short 110 "$line")"
    done < "$LINES"
    echo
    echo "  number or text: select/narrow    r: show all    e: edit location    q: quit"
    echo
}

# resolve_choice <choice>
# Chooses a command from the current list in $LINES.
# Returns: 0 = one command selected (CHOSEN_N/CHOSEN_LINE set),
#          2 = several matches: $LINES narrowed to them, FILTER updated,
#          1 = no match or invalid input.
resolve_choice() {
    CHOSEN_N=''
    CHOSEN_LINE=''
    case $1 in
        *[!0-9]*)   # text fragment: search the current list, case-insensitive
            n=$(awk -v q="$1" 'BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
                q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print NR }' "$LINES")
            if [ -z "$n" ]; then
                echo "No command matches '$1'."
                return 1
            fi
            count=$(printf '%s\n' "$n" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')
            if [ "$count" -eq 1 ]; then
                CHOSEN_N=$n
                CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$CHOSEN_N")
                return 0
            fi
            # several matches: narrow the list to exactly those lines
            filter_list "$1"
            FILTER=$1
            echo "Narrowed to $TOTAL matching commands."
            return 2
            ;;
        *)          # explicit number in the current list
            CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$1")
            if [ -z "$CHOSEN_LINE" ]; then
                echo "Invalid selection (expected 1-$TOTAL)."
                return 1
            fi
            CHOSEN_N=$1
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
}

# run_selected
# Prints what is about to run, then starts it with sh exactly as written.
run_selected() {
    echo
    echo "Running #$CHOSEN_N -- $(model_label "$CHOSEN_LINE"):"
    echo "  $CHOSEN_LINE"
    echo
    exec sh -c "$CHOSEN_LINE"
}

# --- Optional direct selection from the command line -----------------------
if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    resolve_choice "$1"
    rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
        run_selected
    fi
    # rc 1/2: fall through to the menu (the list may now be narrowed)
fi

# --- Interactive menu loop --------------------------------------------------
while :; do
    print_menu
    printf 'Select a number or text fragment (r: show all, e: edit, q: quit): '
    read -r choice || exit 0
    case $choice in
        q | Q | quit) exit 0 ;;
        e | E)
            echo
            echo "Edit the COMMANDS string (line $EDIT_LINE) in:"
            echo "  $SELF"
            echo
            ;;
        r | R)
            FILTER=''
            filter_list ''
            ;;
        '') continue ;;
        *)
            resolve_choice "$choice"
            rc=$?
            if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
                run_selected
            fi
            echo
            ;;
    esac
done

#!/bin/sh
# =============================================================================
#  pick-model.sh -- single-file launcher for the llama.cpp server commands
#
#  EDITING: all launch commands live in the COMMANDS string near the top of
#  this file. Add, remove or change lines there; the menu adapts
#  automatically because the string is re-read from this file each time the
#  script starts.
#
#  Rules for the COMMANDS string:
#    * one command per line (no backslash line continuations)
#    * blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored
#    * the string is a quoted heredoc (<<'COMMANDS_EOF'), so its contents
#      are taken completely literally: single quotes, double quotes, $ and
#      backticks are all safe inside it
#
#  The selected command is executed VERBATIM by sh: no parameter is ever
#  parsed, reordered or modified, so the commands work exactly as written.
#
#  Usage:
#    ./pick-model.sh            interactive menu
#    ./pick-model.sh 3          run command number 3 directly
#    ./pick-model.sh gemma      run the command containing "gemma"
#                               (case-insensitive); if several commands
#                               match, a menu narrowed to them is shown
#
#  Inside the menu you can type:
#    number          run that command
#    text fragment   narrow the list to matching commands (case-insensitive);
#                    a unique match runs immediately
#    r               show all commands again (clears the narrowing)
#    e               show where to edit the COMMANDS string
#    q               quit
#
#  The commands use relative paths (./cuda/..., ./models/...), so this
#  script always starts from the directory it lives in.
# =============================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  COMMANDS -- edit this block freely (one command per line)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
COMMANDS=$(cat <<'COMMANDS_EOF'
./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-F16-qwen3.8-27B.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --image-min-tokens 1024 -ngl 99 -sm tensor -fit off -c 262144 -b 512 -ub 512 --reasoning-preserve -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B-f16.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --image-min-tokens 1024 -ngl 99 -sm tensor -fit off -c 262144 -b 512 -ub 512 --reasoning-preserve -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/Qwen3.8-27B-pi-Q4_K_M.gguf -md ./models/mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-pi-Q4_0.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-Qwen3.8-27B-pi-BF16.gguf --spec-draft-n-max 3 --image-min-tokens 1024 -ngl 99 -sm tensor -fit off -c 262144 -b 512 -ub 512 --reasoning-preserve -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/gemma-4-31B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-BF16_gemma31b.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --model-draft ./models/mtp-gemma-4-31B-it.gguf --spec-draft-n-max 3 -ngl 99 -c 32768 -b 256 -ub 256 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/gemma-4-12b-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --model-draft ./models/mtp-gemma-4-12b-it.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-BF16.gguf -c 262144 -ngl 999 -sm layer -ts 1,1 -fa 1 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 12 -np 1 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --reasoning-budget 0 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'
COMMANDS_EOF
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Script body -- nothing below this line normally needs to be changed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

set -u

# Run from this script's directory (the commands use ./cuda and ./models).
SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd) || exit 1
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR" || exit 1
SELF="$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")"
EDIT_LINE=$(awk '/^COMMANDS=/ { print NR; exit }' "$SELF")

LINES=$(mktemp 2>/dev/null) || LINES="./.pick-model-tmp.$$"
: > "$LINES" || exit 1
trap 'rm -f "$LINES"' EXIT INT TERM

# FILTER: active text narrowing ('' = all commands).
FILTER=''
TOTAL=0

# filter_list [pattern]
# Rebuilds $LINES from the COMMANDS string. Without a pattern it contains
# all command lines; with a pattern only the lines that contain it
# (case-insensitive). Updates TOTAL.
filter_list() {
    if [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$COMMANDS" | awk '
            { sub(/\r$/, "") }          # CRLF safety only, nothing else
            /^[ \t]*$/                  { next }   # skip blank lines
            /^[ \t]*#/                  { next }   # skip comments
            { print }
        ' > "$LINES"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$COMMANDS" | awk -v q="$1" '
            BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
            { sub(/\r$/, "") }
            /^[ \t]*$/                  { next }
            /^[ \t]*#/                  { next }
            q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print }
        ' > "$LINES"
    fi
    TOTAL=$(wc -l < "$LINES" | tr -d '[:space:]')
}

filter_list ''
if [ "$TOTAL" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "error: no launch commands found in the COMMANDS string at the top." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# model_label <line>
# Prints the value of the -m flag of <line>, or the program name if -m is
# absent. Used only for the menu display; the command itself is untouched.
model_label() {
    lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/.*[[:space:]]\{1,\}-m[[:space:]]\{1,\}\([^[:space:]]\{1,\}\).*/\1/p')
    if [ -z "$lbl" ]; then
        lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '{print $1}')
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$lbl"
}

# short <maxchars> <text>
# Prints <text> truncated to <maxchars> characters (with "..." when cut).
short() {
    t=$(printf '%s' "$2" | cut -c1-"$1")
    if [ "$(printf '%s' "$2" | wc -c | tr -d '[:space:]')" -gt "$1" ]; then
        t="$t..."
    fi
    printf '%s' "$t"
}

# line_for_number <n>
# Prints line number <n> (1-based) of the current list; empty if out of range.
line_for_number() {
    case $1 in
        '' | *[!0-9]*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    if [ "$1" -ge 1 ] && [ "$1" -le "$TOTAL" ]; then
        sed -n "$1p" "$LINES"
    fi
}

# print_menu
# Lists the current (possibly narrowed) command list.
print_menu() {
    if [ -z "$FILTER" ]; then
        echo "Available commands ($TOTAL):"
    else
        echo "Commands matching '$FILTER' ($TOTAL):"
    fi
    echo
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        lbl=$(model_label "$line")
        printf ' %2d) %s\n' "$i" "${lbl##*/}"
        printf '      %s\n' "$(short 110 "$line")"
    done < "$LINES"
    echo
    echo "  number or text: select/narrow    r: show all    e: edit location    q: quit"
    echo
}

# resolve_choice <choice>
# Chooses a command from the current list in $LINES.
# Returns: 0 = one command selected (CHOSEN_N/CHOSEN_LINE set),
#          2 = several matches: $LINES narrowed to them, FILTER updated,
#          1 = no match or invalid input.
resolve_choice() {
    CHOSEN_N=''
    CHOSEN_LINE=''
    case $1 in
        *[!0-9]*)   # text fragment: search the current list, case-insensitive
            n=$(awk -v q="$1" 'BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
                q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print NR }' "$LINES")
            if [ -z "$n" ]; then
                echo "No command matches '$1'."
                return 1
            fi
            count=$(printf '%s\n' "$n" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')
            if [ "$count" -eq 1 ]; then
                CHOSEN_N=$n
                CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$CHOSEN_N")
                return 0
            fi
            # several matches: narrow the list to exactly those lines
            filter_list "$1"
            FILTER=$1
            echo "Narrowed to $TOTAL matching commands."
            return 2
            ;;
        *)          # explicit number in the current list
            CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$1")
            if [ -z "$CHOSEN_LINE" ]; then
                echo "Invalid selection (expected 1-$TOTAL)."
                return 1
            fi
            CHOSEN_N=$1
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
}

# run_selected
# Prints what is about to run, then starts it with sh exactly as written.
run_selected() {
    echo
    echo "Running #$CHOSEN_N -- $(model_label "$CHOSEN_LINE"):"
    echo "  $CHOSEN_LINE"
    echo
    exec sh -c "$CHOSEN_LINE"
}

# --- Optional direct selection from the command line -----------------------
if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    resolve_choice "$1"
    rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
        run_selected
    fi
    # rc 1/2: fall through to the menu (the list may now be narrowed)
fi

# --- Interactive menu loop --------------------------------------------------
while :; do
    print_menu
    printf 'Select a number or text fragment (r: show all, e: edit, q: quit): '
    read -r choice || exit 0
    case $choice in
        q | Q | quit) exit 0 ;;
        e | E)
            echo
            echo "Edit the COMMANDS string (line $EDIT_LINE) in:"
            echo "  $SELF"
            echo
            ;;
        r | R)
            FILTER=''
            filter_list ''
            ;;
        '') continue ;;
        *)
            resolve_choice "$choice"
            rc=$?
            if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
                run_selected
            fi
            echo
            ;;
    esac
done

#!/bin/sh
# pick-model.sh
#
# Interactive launcher for the llama.cpp commands stored in launcher.sh.
#
# How it works
#   * On every start it re-reads the command file, so commands you add,
#     remove or comment out are picked up immediately ("real time") --
#     this script never has to be updated when the command list changes.
#   * The selected command is executed VERBATIM: the exact line text is
#     handed to sh, so no parameter is ever parsed, reordered or modified.
#   * Commands must be one line each (no backslash continuations).
#     Blank lines and lines starting with '#' (including the shebang)
#     are ignored.
#
# Usage
#   ./pick-model.sh            show the menu and pick interactively
#   ./pick-model.sh 3          run command number 3 directly
#   ./pick-model.sh gemma      run the single command containing "gemma"
#                              (case-insensitive search); if several match,
#                              the interactive menu is shown instead
#
# The command file defaults to launcher.sh next to this script;
# override it with the environment variable LLAMA_COMMANDS.

set -u

# The commands use relative paths (./cuda/llama-server, ./models/...),
# so always run from the directory that contains this script.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1

COMMAND_FILE="${LLAMA_COMMANDS:-launcher.sh}"

if [ ! -f "$COMMAND_FILE" ]; then
    echo "error: command file '$COMMAND_FILE' not found in $(pwd)." >&2
    echo "       Add your llama-server commands there, one per line." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Working copy holding only the executable lines, in their original order.
# awk guarantees a trailing newline per line, even if the source file's
# last line lacks one, so line numbering stays exact.
LINES=$(mktemp 2>/dev/null) || LINES="./.pick-model-tmp.$$"
: > "$LINES" || exit 1
trap 'rm -f "$LINES"' EXIT INT TERM

awk '{
    sub(/\r$/, "")                    # CRLF safety only, nothing else
    if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*$/) next         # skip blank lines
    if ($0 ~ /^[ \t]*#/) next         # skip comments (incl. shebang)
    print
}' "$COMMAND_FILE" > "$LINES"

TOTAL=$(wc -l < "$LINES" | tr -d '[:space:]')
if [ "$TOTAL" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "error: no launch commands found in $COMMAND_FILE." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# model_label <line>
# Prints the value of the -m flag of <line>, or the program name if -m is
# absent. Used only for the menu display; the command itself is untouched.
model_label() {
    lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/.*[[:space:]]\{1,\}-m[[:space:]]\{1,\}\([^[:space:]]\{1,\}\).*/\1/p')
    if [ -z "$lbl" ]; then
        lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '{print $1}')
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$lbl"
}

# short <maxchars> <text>
# Prints <text> truncated to <maxchars> characters (with "..." when cut).
short() {
    t=$(printf '%s' "$2" | cut -c1-"$1")
    if [ "$(printf '%s' "$2" | wc -c | tr -d '[:space:]')" -gt "$1" ]; then
        t="$t..."
    fi
    printf '%s' "$t"
}

# line_for_number <n>
# Prints line number <n> (1-based) of the command list; empty if out of range.
line_for_number() {
    case $1 in
        '' | *[!0-9]*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    if [ "$1" -ge 1 ] && [ "$1" -le "$TOTAL" ]; then
        sed -n "$1p" "$LINES"
    fi
}

# print_menu
# Lists all commands with a number and the model each one loads.
print_menu() {
    echo "Available commands in $COMMAND_FILE ($TOTAL):"
    echo
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        lbl=$(model_label "$line")
        printf ' %2d) %s\n' "$i" "${lbl##*/}"
        printf '      %s\n' "$(short 110 "$line")"
    done < "$LINES"
    echo
}

# resolve_choice <choice>
# Turns a number or a text fragment into CHOSEN_N / CHOSEN_LINE.
# Succeeds only when exactly one command is selected.
resolve_choice() {
    CHOSEN_N=''
    CHOSEN_LINE=''
    case $1 in
        *[!0-9]*)   # text fragment: search all commands, case-insensitive
            n=$(awk -v q="$1" 'BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
                q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print NR }' "$LINES")
            if [ -z "$n" ]; then
                echo "No command matches '$1'."
                return 1
            fi
            count=$(printf '%s\n' "$n" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')
            if [ "$count" -gt 1 ]; then
                echo "Several commands match '$1' (numbers: $(printf '%s ' $n)). Pick one:"
                return 1
            fi
            CHOSEN_N=$n
            ;;
        *)          # explicit number
            CHOSEN_N=$1
            ;;
    esac
    CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$CHOSEN_N")
    if [ -z "$CHOSEN_LINE" ]; then
        echo "Invalid selection."
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# run_selected
# Prints what is about to run, then starts it with sh exactly as written.
run_selected() {
    echo
    echo "Running #$CHOSEN_N -- $(model_label "$CHOSEN_LINE"):"
    echo "  $CHOSEN_LINE"
    echo
    exec sh -c "$CHOSEN_LINE"
}

# --- Optional direct selection from the command line -----------------------
if [ "$#" -ge 1 ] && resolve_choice "$1"; then
    run_selected
fi

# --- Interactive menu loop --------------------------------------------------
# (The file was parsed at startup, so the menu always reflects the file's
# current contents: edit launcher.sh, run pick-model.sh again.)
while :; do
    print_menu
    printf 'Select a number, a fragment of the command, or q to quit: '
    read -r choice || exit 0
    case $choice in
        q | Q | quit) exit 0 ;;
        '') continue ;;
    esac
    if resolve_choice "$choice"; then
        run_selected
    fi
    echo
done

            echo "Narrowed to $TOTAL matching commands."
            return 2
            ;;
        *)          # explicit number in the current list
            CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$1")
            if [ -z "$CHOSEN_LINE" ]; then
                echo "Invalid selection (expected 1-$TOTAL)."
                return 1
            fi
            CHOSEN_N=$1
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
}

# run_selected
# Prints what is about to run, then starts it with sh exactly as written.
run_selected() {
    echo
    echo "Running #$CHOSEN_N -- $(model_label "$CHOSEN_LINE"):"
    echo "  $CHOSEN_LINE"
    echo
    exec sh -c "$CHOSEN_LINE"
}

# --- Optional direct selection from the command line -----------------------
if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    resolve_choice "$1"
    rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
        run_selected
    fi
    # rc 1/2: fall through to the menu (the list may now be narrowed)
fi

# --- Interactive menu loop --------------------------------------------------
while :; do
    print_menu
    printf 'Select a number or text fragment (r: show all, e: edit, q: quit): '
    read -r choice || exit 0
    case $choice in
        q | Q | quit) exit 0 ;;
        e | E)
            echo
            echo "Edit the COMMANDS string (line $EDIT_LINE) in:"
            echo "  $SELF"
            echo
            ;;
        r | R)
            FILTER=''
            filter_list ''
            ;;
        '') continue ;;
        *)
            resolve_choice "$choice"
            rc=$?
            if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
                run_selected
            fi
            echo
            ;;
    esac
done

#!/bin/sh
# =============================================================================
#  pick-model.sh -- single-file launcher for the llama.cpp server commands
#
#  EDITING: all launch commands live in the COMMANDS string near the top of
#  this file. Add, remove or change lines there; the menu adapts
#  automatically because the string is re-read from this file each time the
#  script starts.
#
#  Rules for the COMMANDS string:
#    * one command per line (no backslash line continuations)
#    * blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored
#    * the string is a quoted heredoc (<<'COMMANDS_EOF'), so its contents
#      are taken completely literally: single quotes, double quotes, $ and
#      backticks are all safe inside it
#
#  The selected command is executed VERBATIM by sh: no parameter is ever
#  parsed, reordered or modified, so the commands work exactly as written.
#
#  Usage:
#    ./pick-model.sh            interactive menu
#    ./pick-model.sh 3          run command number 3 directly
#    ./pick-model.sh gemma      run the command containing "gemma"
#                               (case-insensitive); if several commands
#                               match, a menu narrowed to them is shown
#
#  Inside the menu you can type:
#    number          run that command
#    text fragment   narrow the list to matching commands (case-insensitive);
#                    a unique match runs immediately
#    r               show all commands again (clears the narrowing)
#    e               show where to edit the COMMANDS string
#    q               quit
#
#  The commands use relative paths (./cuda/..., ./models/...), so this
#  script always starts from the directory it lives in.
# =============================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  COMMANDS -- edit this block freely (one command per line)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
COMMANDS=$(cat <<'COMMANDS_EOF'
./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-F16-qwen3.8-27B.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --image-min-tokens 1024 -ngl 99 -sm tensor -fit off -c 262144 -b 512 -ub 512 --reasoning-preserve -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-ThinkingCap-Qwen3.8-27B-f16.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --image-min-tokens 1024 -ngl 99 -sm tensor -fit off -c 262144 -b 512 -ub 512 --reasoning-preserve -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/Qwen3.8-27B-pi-Q4_K_M.gguf -md ./models/mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-pi-Q4_0.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-Qwen3.8-27B-pi-BF16.gguf --spec-draft-n-max 3 --image-min-tokens 1024 -ngl 99 -sm tensor -fit off -c 262144 -b 512 -ub 512 --reasoning-preserve -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/gemma-4-31B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-BF16_gemma31b.gguf --spec-type draft-mtp --model-draft ./models/mtp-gemma-4-31B-it.gguf --spec-draft-n-max 3 -ngl 99 -c 32768 -b 256 -ub 256 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --cors-origins "*"

./cuda/llama-server -m ./models/gemma-4-12b-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --model-draft ./models/mtp-gemma-4-12b-it.gguf --mmproj ./models/mmproj-BF16.gguf -c 262144 -ngl 999 -sm layer -ts 1,1 -fa 1 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -t 12 -np 1 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 1234 --reasoning-budget 0 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'
COMMANDS_EOF
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Script body -- nothing below this line normally needs to be changed.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

set -u

# Run from this script's directory (the commands use ./cuda and ./models).
SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd) || exit 1
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR" || exit 1
SELF="$SCRIPT_DIR/$(basename "$0")"
EDIT_LINE=$(awk '/^COMMANDS=/ { print NR; exit }' "$SELF")

LINES=$(mktemp 2>/dev/null) || LINES="./.pick-model-tmp.$$"
: > "$LINES" || exit 1
trap 'rm -f "$LINES"' EXIT INT TERM

# FILTER: active text narrowing ('' = all commands).
FILTER=''
TOTAL=0

# filter_list [pattern]
# Rebuilds $LINES from the COMMANDS string. Without a pattern it contains
# all command lines; with a pattern only the lines that contain it
# (case-insensitive). Updates TOTAL.
filter_list() {
    if [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$COMMANDS" | awk '
            { sub(/\r$/, "") }          # CRLF safety only, nothing else
            /^[ \t]*$/                  { next }   # skip blank lines
            /^[ \t]*#/                  { next }   # skip comments
            { print }
        ' > "$LINES"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$COMMANDS" | awk -v q="$1" '
            BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
            { sub(/\r$/, "") }
            /^[ \t]*$/                  { next }
            /^[ \t]*#/                  { next }
            q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print }
        ' > "$LINES"
    fi
    TOTAL=$(wc -l < "$LINES" | tr -d '[:space:]')
}

filter_list ''
if [ "$TOTAL" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "error: no launch commands found in the COMMANDS string at the top." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# model_label <line>
# Prints the value of the -m flag of <line>, or the program name if -m is
# absent. Used only for the menu display; the command itself is untouched.
model_label() {
    lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -n 's/.*[[:space:]]\{1,\}-m[[:space:]]\{1,\}\([^[:space:]]\{1,\}\).*/\1/p')
    if [ -z "$lbl" ]; then
        lbl=$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '{print $1}')
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$lbl"
}

# short <maxchars> <text>
# Prints <text> truncated to <maxchars> characters (with "..." when cut).
short() {
    t=$(printf '%s' "$2" | cut -c1-"$1")
    if [ "$(printf '%s' "$2" | wc -c | tr -d '[:space:]')" -gt "$1" ]; then
        t="$t..."
    fi
    printf '%s' "$t"
}

# line_for_number <n>
# Prints line number <n> (1-based) of the current list; empty if out of range.
line_for_number() {
    case $1 in
        '' | *[!0-9]*) return 0 ;;
    esac
    if [ "$1" -ge 1 ] && [ "$1" -le "$TOTAL" ]; then
        sed -n "$1p" "$LINES"
    fi
}

# print_menu
# Lists the current (possibly narrowed) command list.
print_menu() {
    if [ -z "$FILTER" ]; then
        echo "Available commands ($TOTAL):"
    else
        echo "Commands matching '$FILTER' ($TOTAL):"
    fi
    echo
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        lbl=$(model_label "$line")
        printf ' %2d) %s\n' "$i" "${lbl##*/}"
        printf '      %s\n' "$(short 110 "$line")"
    done < "$LINES"
    echo
    echo "  number or text: select/narrow    r: show all    e: edit location    q: quit"
    echo
}

# resolve_choice <choice>
# Chooses a command from the current list in $LINES.
# Returns: 0 = one command selected (CHOSEN_N/CHOSEN_LINE set),
#          2 = several matches: $LINES narrowed to them, FILTER updated,
#          1 = no match or invalid input.
resolve_choice() {
    CHOSEN_N=''
    CHOSEN_LINE=''
    case $1 in
        *[!0-9]*)   # text fragment: search the current list, case-insensitive
            n=$(awk -v q="$1" 'BEGIN { q = tolower(q) }
                q != "" && index(tolower($0), q) { print NR }' "$LINES")
            if [ -z "$n" ]; then
                echo "No command matches '$1'."
                return 1
            fi
            count=$(printf '%s\n' "$n" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')
            if [ "$count" -eq 1 ]; then
                CHOSEN_N=$n
                CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$CHOSEN_N")
                return 0
            fi
            # several matches: narrow the list to exactly those lines
            filter_list "$1"
            FILTER=$1
            echo "Narrowed to $TOTAL matching commands."
            return 2
            ;;
        *)          # explicit number in the current list
            CHOSEN_LINE=$(line_for_number "$1")
            if [ -z "$CHOSEN_LINE" ]; then
                echo "Invalid selection (expected 1-$TOTAL)."
                return 1
            fi
            CHOSEN_N=$1
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
}

# run_selected
# Prints what is about to run, then starts it with sh exactly as written.
run_selected() {
    echo
    echo "Running #$CHOSEN_N -- $(model_label "$CHOSEN_LINE"):"
    echo "  $CHOSEN_LINE"
    echo
    exec sh -c "$CHOSEN_LINE"
}

# --- Optional direct selection from the command line -----------------------
if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    resolve_choice "$1"
    rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
        run_selected
    fi
    # rc 1/2: fall through to the menu (the list may now be narrowed)
fi

# --- Interactive menu loop --------------------------------------------------
while :; do
    print_menu
    printf 'Select a number or text fragment (r: show all, e: edit, q: quit): '
    read -r choice || exit 0
    case $choice in
        q | Q | quit) exit 0 ;;
        e | E)
            echo
            echo "Edit the COMMANDS string (line $EDIT_LINE) in:"
            echo "  $SELF"
            echo
            ;;
        r | R)
            FILTER=''
            filter_list ''
            ;;
        '') continue ;;
        *)
            resolve_choice "$choice"
            rc=$?
            if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
                run_selected
            fi
            echo
            ;;
    esac
done
